reason: For the given input exactly one of the two disjoint-bitmask writes reaches the SRAM. The update D1/NoUs is drained at N+1, but the same cycle's setIdx hit overwrites the buffer entry with the sweep write D2/Us while the drain clears needWrite for that same entry (WriteBuffer.scala:176 vs :227, both take effect at the same edge), so the sweep write is parked with needWrite=0 and is discarded when the next sweep set (S+1) allocates entry 0. Set S of bank B therefore ends with D1's tag/cnt/target but with the usefulCnt bits that were in the SRAM before the sweep (D1 carried NoUs, which excludes bits < UsefulCntWidth per IttageTable.scala:177-179), not usefulCnt=0 as required. No other path repairs it: the reset sweep does not revisit S, and a later update to S with usefulCntValid=1 writes io.update.usefulCnt, not necessarily 0. Severity is bounded (one set per coincidence, corrected only by the next tick-triggered sweep), but the required result is violated.
reachability: reachable under default IttageParameters (NumBanks=2, TableWriteBufferSize=4, UsefulCntWidth=1, ittage/Parameters.scala:31-39) because: needReset stays 1 across intervening update cycles (IttageTable.scala:185-189), so updates during a sweep are ordinary; io.update.valid=RegNext(updateMask) is a single-cycle pulse per training branch (Ittage.scala:401), so valid at N and not at N+1 is normal; usefulCntValid=0 is produced by the alt-provider update path (Ittage.scala:338-346, :409); io.req.valid=s1_fire&&s1_isIndirect (Ittage.scala:191) is idle on any cycle without an indirect fetch, which is what makes N+1 a sweep cycle, and a sweep cycle by construction has io.req.fire=0 on all banks (:182), so a pending entry is always drainable exactly when the sweep write hits it; updateIdx===resetSet is a 1/setsPerBank coincidence per update during a sweep (setsPerBank=128 or 256 for the default tables), i.e. a plain hash/counter collision with no guard against it.
